nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and let $G$ be a finite $C_\pi$-group. Then every subgroup $K$ of $G$ that contains a Hall $\pi$-subgroup of $G$ is itself a $C_\pi$-group. This answers Kourovka Problem 17.44(a) in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Overgroups of Hall subgroups in $C_\pi$-groups (Vdovin–Revin)

nodes.summary: The statement, posed by E. P. Vdovin and D. O. Revin, that for every set $\pi$ of natural numbers and every finite $C_\pi$-group $G$, every subgroup $K$ of $G$ that contains a Hall $\pi$-subgroup of $G$ is itself a $C_\pi$-group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.44(a): overgroups of Hall subgroups in $C_\pi$-groups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and let $G$ be a finite $D_\pi$-group. Then every subgroup $K$ of $G$ that contains a Hall $\pi$-subgroup of $G$ is itself a $D_\pi$-group. This answers Kourovka Problem 17.44(b) in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Overgroups of Hall subgroups in $D_\pi$-groups (Manzaeva, Vdovin–Manzaeva–Revin)

nodes.summary: The statement, posed by E. P. Vdovin and D. O. Revin, that for every set $\pi$ of natural numbers and every finite $D_\pi$-group $G$, every subgroup $K$ of $G$ that contains a Hall $\pi$-subgroup of $G$ is itself a $D_\pi$-group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.44(b): overgroups of Hall subgroups in $D_\pi$-groups

nodes.summary: For all sets $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ of natural numbers, every finite group that has a Hall $\pi_1$-subgroup and a Hall $\pi_2$-subgroup also has a Hall $(\pi_1 \cap \pi_2)$-subgroup; that is, writing $E_\pi$ for the class of finite groups with a Hall $\pi$-subgroup, $E_{\pi_1} \cap E_{\pi_2}$ is contained in $E_{\pi_1 \cap \pi_2}$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroups exist for intersections of prime sets

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for all sets $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ of natural numbers, every finite group that has a Hall $\pi_1$-subgroup and a Hall $\pi_2$-subgroup also has a Hall $(\pi_1 \cap \pi_2)$-subgroup; that is, writing $E_\pi$ for the class of finite groups with a Hall $\pi$-subgroup, $E_{\pi_1} \cap E_{\pi_2}$ is contained in $E_{\pi_1 \cap \pi_2}$.
nodes.title: Zavarnitsine's question on Hall subgroups for intersections of prime sets

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A group $G$ belongs to the class $E_\pi$ when $G$ has a Hall $\pi$-subgroup.
nodes.title: The class $E_\pi$ of groups with a Hall π-subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A group $G$ is a $C_\pi$-group when it has a Hall $\pi$-subgroup and any two Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ are conjugate, that is, $K = gHg^{-1}$ for some $g \in G$.
nodes.title: $C_\pi$-group

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A group $G$ is a $D_\pi$-group when any two maximal $\pi$-subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ are conjugate, that is, $K = gHg^{-1}$ for some $g \in G$.
nodes.title: $D_\pi$-group

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A group $G$ is a $D_\pi$-group when any two maximal $\pi$-subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ are conjugate, that is, $K = gHg^{-1}$ for some $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Dπ-groups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers (only the primes in $\pi$ matter). A group $G$ is a $D_\pi$-group (Kourovka Archive 3.62) when $G$ has a Hall $\pi$-subgroup, any two Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ are conjugate ($K = gHg^{-1}$ for some $g \in G$), and every subgroup of $G$ whose order is a $\pi$-number lies in some Hall $\pi$-subgroup. Here the order of an infinite subgroup is taken to be $0$, which…
nodes.title: $D_\pi$-groups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall $\pi$-subgroup when its order $|H|$ is a $\pi$-number and no prime dividing its index $|G : H|$ lies in $\pi$. Here an infinite order or index is taken to be $0$, which every prime divides.
nodes.title: Hall $\pi$-subgroups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and $G$ a group. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is a Hall $\pi$-subgroup when its order $|H|$ is a $\pi$-number and no prime divisor of its index $|G : H|$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: Hall $\pi$-subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $G$. Then $H$ is a Hall $\pi$-subgroup when its order $|H|$ is a $\pi$-number and no prime divisor of its index $|G : H|$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: Hall π-subgroups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall $\pi$-subgroup when it is a $\pi$-subgroup and no prime divisor of its index $|G : H|$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: Hall π-subgroups (Kourovka 18.31)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and $G$ a group. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is a maximal $\pi$-subgroup when its order $|H|$ is a $\pi$-number and every subgroup $L$ of $G$ that contains $H$ and whose order is a $\pi$-number equals $H$.
nodes.title: Maximal $\pi$-subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a maximal $\pi$-subgroup when it is a $\pi$-subgroup and every $\pi$-subgroup $K$ of $G$ containing $H$ equals $H$.
nodes.title: Maximal π-subgroups (Kourovka 18.31)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A natural number $n$ is a $\pi$-number when every prime dividing $n$ lies in $\pi$.

nodes.summary: Kourovka Problem 13.33 has a positive answer: for every set $\pi$ of natural numbers, every normal subgroup of a finite $D_\pi$-group is itself a $D_\pi$-group.
nodes.title: Normal subgroups of finite $D_\pi$-groups are $D_\pi$-groups

nodes.summary: This is the proposition (F. Gross) that for every set $\pi$ of natural numbers, every normal subgroup of a finite $D_\pi$-group is itself a $D_\pi$-group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.33

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. For a group $G$, the $\pi$-core $O_\pi(G)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by all normal $\pi$-subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: The π-core

nodes.summary: It is not the case that for every set $\pi$ of natural numbers every finite $D_\pi$-group $G$ has Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H_1$, $H_2$, $H_3$ with $H_1 \cap H_2 \cap H_3 = O_\pi(G)$, the $\pi$-core of $G$: the answer to Kourovka 18.31 is negative.
nodes.title: Three Hall π-subgroups need not meet in the π-core

nodes.summary: For every set $\pi$ of natural numbers and every finite $D_\pi$-group $G$, there are Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H_1$, $H_2$, $H_3$ of $G$, not necessarily distinct, with $H_1 \cap H_2 \cap H_3 = O_\pi(G)$, the $\pi$-core of $G$.
nodes.title: Three Hall π-subgroups meeting in the π-core (Kourovka 18.31)
